title: D1 deeper finding: freed topbar space never reaches the log
body: At 390x844 on 791b553 with the hide active: topbar 62, viewscreen 135, stations 154, console 378 = log-row 84px floor + commands 288 + gap; log visible 62px, UNCHANGED from pre-P2. The ~87px freed by the topbar fix flows to the stations block (internal-scroll area), not the log - the console row sits at its min-content (commands-dominated) and the 1fr log row never grows. D1's goal (log comfortably in view) requires bounding stations harder at <=900px (or compressing the commands stack) so freed space reaches the log row. Routed to executor as a disclosed execution-time fork.

context: Post-791b553, pre-fix commit. Orchestrator premise-gate verdict at 390x844: chips visible (3/3) but vs-foot CLIPPED (bottom 322 vs viewscreen bottom 230) -> per T1.4 the G1 hide must not ship; G3 flip is plan-sanctioned, not this fork. THIS fork is the deeper measured finding: with the topbar space freed, .log still showed only ~62px at 390x844. Measured: topbar 62, viewscreen 135, stations 154, console 378 (grid rows resolved 84px log + 288px commands), bridge 691, app 707. The freed ~87px flowed into the stations block (already internally scrolling), not the log — the console row sits at min-content (commands-dominated 288px) and the minmax(84px,1fr) log row never grows past its floor. D1's goal (log comfortably in view on phones) needs the freed space to actually reach the log. The plan did not anticipate this: an execution-time, load-bearing fork.

options.a: Bound the stacked stations harder at <=900px: max-height clamp(140px,24vh,240px) -> clamp(96px,14vh,160px). Stations already scroll internally, so nothing is lost, only hidden behind scroll. Frees ~36px at 844 tall (154 -> ~118). COST: station glanceability — fewer crew/supply rows visible before scrolling. Alone: log ~= 84+36 = ~120px, short of the ~150px target.
options.b: Compress the commands stack at <=900px: .commands/.cmd-grid gaps 6->4px, .btn.primary padding 14px->8px + font 17->15px (the exact treatment the max-height:800px block already applies on short desktops), tighter cmd-grid/danger paddings. Every touch floor untouched: 44px cmd-grid/.btn.small, 48px primary. Saves ~40-56px off the 288px commands row. COST: denser command console, smaller primary label. Alone: log ~= 84+40..56 = ~124-140px, still short of ~150px.
options.c: Both (a) and (b), targeting log >= ~150px at 390x844. Arithmetic from the orchestrator's measured numbers: app 707 - viewscreen 135 - stations ~118 (14vh@844) - 2 bridge gaps 12 = console row ~442; commands ~232-248 after compression + 6px console gap -> log ~= 188-204px vs the 62px before (and vs the 84px floor). COST: both costs above, each applied moderately instead of one applied brutally.

justification: Neither mechanism alone reaches the ~150px log target (a: ~120px, b: ~124-140px); c clears it with margin (~188px by arithmetic). Splitting the reclaim keeps each cost moderate: stations keep internal scroll and a 96px floor (header + ~2 rows visible before scrolling), and the commands compression only trims paddings/gaps/font — the 44/48px touch floors are untouched and the harness now pins the 48px primary floor so compression can never silently eat the touch target. Cheap-vs-right, honestly: the CHEAPEST fix was (a) alone with a brutal cap (~10vh) — rejected because it buries the crew/supply glance to buy the last 30px; the 'rightest' fix would let the log row participate directly in the bridge slack (e.g. raising the minmax log floor), but the bridge console row is minmax(min-content,1fr) — a bigger log floor inflates min-content and risks re-opening page scroll on shorter phones (<=700px tall), gambling the Phase-1 no-scroll guarantee, which a remediation must not do. c stays entirely inside the plan's existing internal-scroll pattern and the <=900px block. VERIFICATION HONESTY: this executor has no browser; the ~188px figure is arithmetic from the orchestrator's measured numbers, and the orchestrator's T4.3 evidence pass owns confirming log >= ~150px live. Also shipped in the same commit, per the coordinator's direction and plan T1.4 (not part of this fork): the G3 flip — the #crt:has(.bridge) #topbar-status display:none rule deleted, ellipsis floor kept, harness (h2) now REQUIRES the hide's absence, dashboard/Addendum record the fallback.

title: FORK-D1b parameter tuning (within chosen option c)
body: The fork entry cited stations clamp(96px,14vh,160px) as the (a)-mechanism example. In-browser measurement at 390x844 with 14vh showed log=131px: the commands stack is touch-floor-dominated (54px primary + 8x44px buttons) and compressed to 255px, not the estimated 232-248 - the floors, which are untouchable, set the limit. Shipped tuning, same mechanism: stations clamp vh 14->12 (stations 118->101px) and .bridge gap 6->4px (+4px). Measured result: log=152px at 390x844 (>= ~150 target), no page scroll, min button 44px, primary 54px. Honest added cost vs the fork text: stations show ~2 crew rows instead of ~2.5 before scrolling. No new mechanism introduced; option (c) as logged, parameters tuned to actually meet the target it declared.

reasoning: Both single-lever options proven insufficient against immovable touch floors; combining is the minimum change clearing the 150px target; raising the log floor directly rightly declined (threatens the phase-1 no-page-scroll guarantee).
